key_insight: RPG lets embodied agents improve robot execution without weight updates by iteratively reconstructing skills, practicing in simulation, and revising prompts and a reusable skill library.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to upgrade robot systems with lower retraining cost, faster adaptation, and less human annotation burden across changing manipulation tasks.
method: Mine offline data to identify capabilities and build related practice tasks in simulation.
Use execution feedback, simulator state, and dataset videos to diagnose failures and create/refine symbolic skills.
Cross-test candidate changes, merge only validated revisions, and deploy them through a frozen multimodal LLM controller.
evidence_signal: On 22 held-out manipulation tasks, success rose from 28.6% after the first practice round to 95.0% after 15 rounds, and the frozen system achieved 30/30 successes in physical trials after calibration and hardware adaptation.
watch_item: Performance depends on access to informative offline data, simulator fidelity, and a calibration/adaptation step, so transfer to new robots or poorly modeled tasks may be less reliable.
paper_title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
